ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
The Guru is the embodiment of the Transcendent Lord, the ultimate source of all peace and comfort. This declares the Guru's divine nature and capacity to bestow complete spiritual solace, affirming the Guru as the provider of all true happiness and spiritual fulfillment.

Themes: Guru's divinity, source of peace, spiritual comfort, ultimate solace.
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
This line declares the Divine as the sole provider and creator, the omnipresent architect of all existence. It asserts that the Divine is the ultimate giver of all blessings and the pervasive force within every being, establishing the Divine's absolute sovereignty and all-encompassing nature.

Themes: Divine sovereignty, divine omnipresence, divine creator, ultimate giver, divine sustainer
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
This is a plea to the Divine, the source of all mercy and compassion, to grant the vision of the Divine presence. Beholding the Divine is described as the path to an elevated spiritual state, a life of redemption and true spiritual living. The speaker yearns for this divine sight as the ultimate spiritual attainment.

Themes: Divine mercy, spiritual vision, redemption, elevated consciousness, divine grace.
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
The devotee praises the Divine as the supreme Master, overflowing with all virtues and possessing profound depth of character. This declaration acknowledges the Divine's boundless excellence and unfathomable greatness, affirming an absolute and perfect authority.

Themes: Divine greatness, divine virtues, supreme master, profound depth
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The Divine is the ultimate giver, the generous provider of all sustenance, and no single mouth or individual effort can fully encompass or adequately express the praise due to such a boundless benefactor. The speaker acknowledges the inadequacy of human praise in the face of the Divine's infinite generosity, questioning how one could ever truly laud such a giver.

Themes: Divine generosity, inadequacy of praise, boundless giving, human limitation, divine sustenance
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The devotee, overwhelmed by the Divine's boundless virtues, humbly asks which of the countless excellences to recount and praise. The Divine is the ultimate Master, an infinite treasury of all good qualities, the sustainer of all beings, making any attempt to list them feel inadequate. This is an expression of profound reverence and awe before the Divine's immeasurable greatness.

Themes: Divine virtues, praise, humility, reverence, immeasurability of God
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
This line admonishes the human mind, calling it foolish for its worldly attachments, and warns that when the time of death arrives, no one, not even one's closest family, will offer shelter or companionship for even a moment. It highlights the transient nature of human relationships and the ultimate solitude of the soul's journey, urging a focus on eternal truths rather than fleeting earthly ties.

Themes: impermanence, death, worldly attachment, solitude, spiritual urgency, human folly
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
The instruction here is for the mind to cease its wavering and doubt, reminding it that the Divine is the ultimate fulfiller of all aspirations and desires. It is an admonition to trust completely in the Divine's capacity to provide and to remain steadfast in that faith, rather than being swayed by uncertainty.

Themes: Steadfastness, divine providence, trust in God, fulfillment of desires.
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
This is an instruction to one's own mind, urging it to engage in the loving remembrance (simran) of the Divine, the Lord of the Universe. It is a call to devotion, encouraging the mind to consistently meditate on and praise the Creator. The speaker is admonishing their own consciousness to turn towards spiritual practice.

Themes: simran, devotion, mind, instruction, divine remembrance
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
The speaker instructs their own mind to seek the divine treasure, the source of all comforts and spiritual wealth, internally rather than externally. This admonition emphasizes that the divine presence resides within oneself, making outward searches for spiritual fulfillment futile. The mind is urged to recognize its inherent connection to the divine rather than pursuing worldly or external objects.

Themes: Inner seeking, divine immanence, futility of external search, self-realization, spiritual treasure.
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
This is an admonition to the human mind, calling it deluded for being captivated by worldly appearances and straying from its true path. It questions why the mind allows itself to be misled by maya (worldly attachment), urging it to listen and understand the folly of its current direction. The mind is being told to cease its infatuation with transient sights.

Themes: delusion, maya (worldly attachment), spiritual blindness, straying from the path, admonition
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
This is an instruction to one's own foolish mind, urging it to cultivate humility and surrender. It advises becoming the dust under the feet of those who have meditated on God (simran), implying that such reverence for the devout is a path to divine union and spiritual elevation. The mind is admonished to listen and adopt this posture of ultimate lowliness.

Themes: humility, simran, sangat, spiritual instruction, divine union
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
This declares that true joy and spiritual sovereignty, surpassing the fleeting pleasures of earthly kingdoms, are attained solely through the True Guru's (Satguru's) glance of grace. It asserts that divine favor grants ultimate contentment and spiritual kingship, far exceeding any worldly dominion.

Themes: divine grace, spiritual joy, Satguru, true happiness, liberation, divine favor
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
When the True Guru (the divine teacher) bestows grace, one does not perceive suffering as pain, but rather as a divine lesson or a path to spiritual growth. This state of mind, granted by the Guru's compassion, transforms one's experience of hardship, eliminating the sensation of distress. The Guru's mercy leads to a perspective where adversity is not recognized as suffering.

Themes: True Guru's grace, spiritual perspective, overcoming suffering, divine compassion, inner peace.
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
This declaration celebrates the culmination of spiritual union, where the soul-bride achieves a state of profound inner peace and unwavering stability (sahaj) upon realizing the Divine. It describes the ultimate spiritual attainment, the direct experience of the Lord, as a result of deep devotion and surrender, marking the completion of the soul's journey towards its divine spouse.

Themes: spiritual union, inner peace, divine realization, sahaj, devotion, surrender
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
By propitiating the True Guru, one attains inner peace and fulfills all desires, finding contentment and spiritual solace through alignment with divine wisdom. This is a declaration of the profound benefits of spiritual devotion and surrender to the Guru's guidance.

Themes: spiritual peace, divine contentment, Guru's grace, fulfillment of desires
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
The True Guru (Satguru) is an eternal helper and supporter, perpetually severing the root cause of suffering for all who seek refuge. The Guru eradicates the very banner of pain, offering constant aid and eliminating the source of distress. This declaration praises the Satguru's unwavering assistance and transformative power.

Themes: Divine grace, spiritual liberation, refuge in the Guru, eradication of suffering.
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
This declares that human life is the singular opportunity to merge with the Divine, a precious chance to achieve union with the Lord of the Universe. It emphasizes the unique and fleeting nature of this human birth as the sole pathway to spiritual liberation and connection with the Creator.

Themes: human life, spiritual opportunity, divine union, liberation, preciousness of life
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
Mankind arrives in this world with a singular purpose: to accrue the profit of naam (the divine Name), to gather the spiritual wealth of remembrance, and to earn the true gain of connecting with the Divine. This human birth is an opportunity to accumulate spiritual merit and achieve the ultimate spiritual profit.

Themes: purpose of life, naam simran, spiritual profit, human birth
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
This instruction urges the seeker to meet with the Guru, the divine teacher, and firmly implant devotion to the Divine within their heart. It declares that only this unwavering devotion, cultivated through the Guru's guidance, will ultimately be beneficial and truly serve one's purpose in life. This is a direct command to seek spiritual guidance and cultivate inner piety.

Themes: Devotion, Guru's guidance, spiritual benefit, purpose of life, inner piety.
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
This declares that a truly successful and meaningful life is achieved by continually listening to the divine Name (naam) and engaging in its loving remembrance (simran). Such a life, dedicated to the Divine, transcends mortal limitations and attains eternal spiritual existence. The purpose of human life is to connect with the Divine through constant devotion.

Themes: naam simran, eternal life, purpose of life, spiritual success, divine remembrance
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The beautiful lotus feet of the Divine are the sole support and refuge for the humble devotees, providing a firm foundation and ultimate sanctuary for their lives. This declares that the Divine presence is the only true anchor and sustenance for those who serve with humility.

Themes: Divine presence, refuge, support, devotion, humility, sanctuary
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
This is a plea to the Divine, asking for the grace to enshrine the beautiful lotus feet of the Lord within one's heart, sustained by the support of the perfect Guru. It expresses a deep longing to maintain constant remembrance and devotion, seeking the Guru's guidance as the foundation for this inner spiritual practice. The speaker desires to perpetually serve the Divine presence in their innermost being.

Themes: Devotion, divine grace, Guru's support, inner remembrance, spiritual longing.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
The practice of loving the Divine's lotus feet, a metaphor for complete surrender and devotion to the Divine presence, takes root in the minds of the saints. This way of life, characterized by unwavering affection for the Divine, becomes an inherent part of their spiritual discipline and mental state. It is a path of profound love and dedication that defines the devout.

Themes: Divine love, surrender, devotion, saints, spiritual practice, lotus feet
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
This instruction to the mind urges it to embark upon the divine presence, likening the feet of the Divine to a small, beautiful ship that carries one across the terrifying world-ocean of suffering and rebirth. Taking refuge in the Divine allows one to transcend worldly attachments and achieve liberation.

Themes: Divine refuge, liberation, world-ocean, spiritual journey, devotion
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
When the mind is imbued with the beautiful, tender feet of the Divine, it finds nothing else appealing or sweet. This state of spiritual absorption means that only the remembrance of the Divine brings joy and satisfaction, rendering all worldly pleasures tasteless and insignificant. The soul is completely captivated by the Divine presence.

Themes: Divine devotion, spiritual absorption, detachment from maya, inner contentment, divine love
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
The soul that drinks the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name) achieves lasting spiritual satisfaction and eternal life, transcending the cycles of aging, death, and suffering. This spiritual immortality, bestowed by the Guru, ensures freedom from all worldly afflictions and sorrow.

Themes: naam simran, spiritual immortality, divine grace, freedom from suffering
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Those who drink the naam-ras, the essence of the divine Name, become spiritually intoxicated and liberated. This spiritual rapture breaks the bonds of maya (worldly attachment) and severs the snares of worldly illusion, freeing the soul from all entanglements.

Themes: naam, liberation, spiritual intoxication, freedom from maya
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
The soul that drinks the ambrosial nectar of the divine Name (naam) experiences spiritual rebirth and eternal life. This instruction to one's own mind emphasizes that partaking in the divine essence is the path to true spiritual vitality and everlasting existence.

Themes: naam, ambrosial nectar, spiritual life, immortality, inner instruction
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
This is an instruction to the seeker to drink the divine essence, the naam (the divine Name), by taking refuge in the Guru. It is an exhortation to engage in simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine, urging the listener to immerse themselves in the spiritual nectar that comes from devotion and surrender to the Guru's teachings.

Themes: naam, simran, Guru's refuge, divine essence, spiritual instruction
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
This line declares the transformative power of the Guru's grace, which instills the life-giving naam (the divine Name) into the individual, thereby resurrecting a soul that was spiritually dead. It describes the Guru's action of pouring the ambrosial nectar of the divine Name into one's being, revitalizing and bringing spiritual life to the previously lifeless self. The Guru's intervention grants spiritual rebirth and eternal life.

Themes: Guru's grace, spiritual rebirth, naam simran, divine nectar, spiritual awakening, liberation from spiritual death.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
This line declares that the divine Name (naam) is an ambrosial treasure, a life-giving nectar that bestows immortality and spiritual wealth. It instructs the listener to gather in holy company (sangat) and collectively partake of this naam, urging communal remembrance and shared spiritual nourishment. The instruction is to actively engage with and absorb the divine essence.

Themes: Naam, ambrosial nectar, spiritual treasure, communal worship, divine remembrance.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The Divine liberates individuals from the dread of transmigration, ensuring they are not reborn into the cycle of birth and death. This liberation from the fear of reincarnation is a gift from the Divine, removing the anxiety associated with the endless cycle of existence and granting ultimate release.

Themes: liberation, transmigration, fear of death, divine grace, reincarnation
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Attaining sahaj (intuitive equipoise) leads to the realization of God, which in turn eradicates the fear of death and spiritual demise. This state of inner stability and divine union liberates the soul from the dread of the Messenger of Death, ensuring spiritual immortality.

Themes: sahaj, divine union, fear of death, spiritual liberation, inner peace
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Chanting the praises of the Divine, especially within the company of the devout (sangat), eliminates the fear of birth and death, freeing the soul from the cycle of transmigration. This practice dissolves the existential dread associated with the impermanence of life and the unknown of death, offering liberation through devotion.

Themes: fear of death, liberation, simran, sangat, transmigration, divine praise
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Contemplating the divine through simran (loving remembrance) eliminates the fear of the cycle of birth and death, old age, and suffering. This practice brings liberation from the anxieties of mortal existence, freeing the mind from the dread of aging and the ultimate end of life.

Themes: Simran, liberation from fear, cycle of birth and death, old age, suffering
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
The suffering inherent in the cycle of birth and death is eliminated, and the dread of the Yamaraj (the messenger of death) is dispelled. This declares the liberation from existential suffering and the fear of mortality that comes from spiritual devotion. It describes the ultimate release from worldly anxieties and the cycle of transmigration.

Themes: liberation, freedom from suffering, fear of death, cycle of transmigration, spiritual devotion
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
The speaker declares that the cycle of birth and death, with all its associated anxieties and fears, has ended for them. Through spiritual understanding and divine grace, the dread of reincarnation and mortality has been completely eradicated, bringing liberation from existential terror.

Themes: liberation from samsara, fearlessness, spiritual release, end of transmigration
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Through the sanctuary and support of the sangat (the company of the devout), one cultivates a deep, loving connection with the Divine. Dwelling within the community of the holy enables the soul to develop profound affection and spiritual intimacy with God. This spiritual companionship fosters a loving bond with the Creator.

Themes: sangat, divine love, spiritual connection, community support
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Through the company of the devout (sangat), one can cross the terrifying world-ocean of suffering and transmigration, escaping the noose of death and the cycle of rebirth. This instruction encourages association with holy beings as the path to liberation and freedom from the fear of death.

Themes: sangat, liberation, death, transmigration, spiritual journey, divine grace
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
This declares that spiritual union with the Divine is achieved through the congregation of the devout (sangat). Finding the company of holy beings leads directly to meeting and merging with the Lord, emphasizing the transformative power of communal spiritual practice and the path to divine connection.

Themes: sangat (company of the devout), divine union, spiritual transformation, communal worship, divine presence
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
The devout, immersed in the sacred fellowship of the sangat, are perpetually dyed in the beautiful hue of divine love, continuously singing the praises of the Divine. This describes the blissful and transformative state of those who consistently engage in holy company, highlighting the continuous nature of their devotion and the profound spiritual coloring it imparts.

Themes: sangat, divine love, praise, continuous devotion, spiritual transformation
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
The Divine liberates individuals from worldly vices and attachments, drawing their minds into the Saadh Sangat (the company of the devout). This is a declaration of the Divine's power to rescue souls from the allure of maya (worldly illusion) and guide them towards spiritual community and devotion. It describes the transformative action of the Divine in redirecting human consciousness.

Themes: Divine grace, liberation, Saadh Sangat, spiritual transformation, detachment from vice.
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
This line instructs the listener, addressed as a friend, to attentively consider the profound spiritual benefits and transformative power of associating with the sangat (the company of the devout). It emphasizes that understanding the glory and virtue of holy fellowship is crucial for spiritual progress, urging deep contemplation on the blessings derived from such association.

Themes: sangat (holy company), spiritual instruction, divine glory, attentive listening, spiritual benefit
ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
The speaker yearns to receive the dust from the feet of the Saints, metaphorically seeking the blessings and spiritual wisdom of holy beings. This act of applying the dust to the forehead signifies profound humility, reverence, and a desire to absorb their virtuous qualities, which the speaker considers to be the ultimate treasure and spiritual accomplishment.

Themes: humility, reverence, spiritual wisdom, blessings, devotion to saints
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
This is a plea to the Divine for the spiritual elevation that comes from humble service to the Guru's Sikhs, specifically requesting the dust of their feet as a symbol of utter submission and reverence. The speaker, acknowledging their own sinful nature, seeks this sacred contact as a means to attain a higher spiritual state and liberation from their transgressions. It expresses a profound desire for spiritual upliftment through association with the devout.

Themes: Seeking spiritual elevation, humility, service to the devout, liberation from sin, divine grace.
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
The speaker expresses a deep yearning to join the company of the devout (sangat) and participate in their worship, desiring to sing the praises of the Divine alongside them. This is a plea for inclusion in spiritual community and a declaration of the highest aspiration: to engage in collective remembrance of God's virtues.

Themes: sangat, devotion, divine praise, spiritual aspiration, humility
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
The speaker expresses a profound desire to serve the Divine's devotees, offering to perform humble tasks like cleaning their feet with their hair. This act of extreme humility and self-abnegation demonstrates a deep reverence for those connected to the Divine, seeking to merge with the divine presence through selfless service to its servants. It is a plea for the opportunity to engage in such devoted service.

Themes: Seva (selfless service), humility, devotion, reverence for devotees, spiritual aspiration.
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
The supplicant pleads for the grace of the Divine, asking to be blessed with the dust from the feet of the saints, a metaphor for the humility and spiritual benefit gained from serving and associating with the devout. This is the ultimate peace and spiritual solace that the seeker yearns for, a state of profound contentment found in humble devotion and the company of the holy.

Themes: Divine grace, humility, service, spiritual peace, company of the devout.
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
The speaker expresses a profound longing for complete surrender and humility before the saints, wishing for their forehead to rest at the saints' feet, their eyes to be filled with the blessed vision of their presence, and their body to be covered in the dust from their feet. This is a plea for ultimate devotion and the spiritual purification that comes from association with the devout.

Themes: surrender, humility, devotion, spiritual purification, sangat (company of the devout)
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
This praises the Divine as supremely beautiful and captivating, yet distinct and transcendent amidst all creation. It declares the Beloved to be immanent within everything while simultaneously remaining utterly unique and separate, highlighting the paradox of the Divine's pervasive presence and unparalleled nature. The line implies that meditating on the Divine's praises bestows spiritual life.

Themes: Divine beauty, immanence, transcendence, spiritual life, paradox
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
This declaration praises the Divine, affirming that the Divine Name (naam) is inherently beautiful, the Divine form is beautiful, and the Divine's love is supremely beautiful. It expresses deep admiration and devotion for the aesthetic and spiritual perfection of the Lord, acknowledging the captivating nature of the Divine presence in all its manifestations.

Themes: Divine beauty, naam (Divine Name), Divine love, devotion, spiritual aesthetics.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
The Divine is inherently beautiful, the ultimate source of all spiritual bliss and joy, embodying all sweetness and delight. This declaration praises the Divine's aesthetic and experiential perfection, affirming that all true pleasure and spiritual nectar originate solely from the Divine being.

Themes: Divine beauty, spiritual bliss, source of joy, divine sweetness
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The speaker, addressing her mother, declares that her Beloved, the Divine Master, is supremely beautiful to her eyes, captivating her completely. Gazing upon the Divine, she becomes utterly enchanted and absorbed, experiencing a profound spiritual intoxication and deep longing. Her soul is drawn irresistibly to the Divine presence, finding ultimate satisfaction and bliss in beholding it.

Themes: Divine beauty, spiritual intoxication, longing for God, captivating presence, spiritual absorption.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The Beloved, Merciful Lord of the Universe possesses an infinitely beautiful and boundless glory, a pervasive splendor that extends without limit. This declares the immeasurable and all-encompassing majesty of the Divine.

Themes: Divine glory, infinite nature, boundless splendor, pervasive presence
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine protects and honors its devotees, ensuring their dignity in all circumstances. The Creator personally inspires and enables them to engage in simran (loving remembrance) of the naam (the divine Name), guiding them to spiritual practice and safeguarding their spiritual journey.

Themes: Divine protection, naam simran, divine grace, devotee's honor, spiritual guidance
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Divine, as the cherished Master, consistently safeguards the honor and devotion of its humble servants, having unfailingly protected them across all ages and throughout history. This declaration reassures the faithful that divine protection is an eternal and unwavering principle, always extended to those who live in loving remembrance and service.

Themes: Divine protection, steadfast devotion, eternal grace, spiritual refuge
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
The Divine is the cherished Master of all souls, the beloved life-force for all devotees. The Divine is dear to all who practice loving devotion, and in turn, all devotees are dear to the Divine. This establishes a reciprocal relationship of love and affection between the Divine and those who worship with devotion.

Themes: Divine love, devotion, reciprocal relationship, soul's master, cherished presence.
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
The divine Name (naam) is the sole support and refuge for all devotees and saints, providing unwavering strength and shelter. The Creator, through the naam, sustains and protects those who dedicate themselves to spiritual life, offering a constant anchor in an impermanent world. This declaration affirms the ultimate reliance of the devout on the divine presence.

Themes: Divine support, spiritual refuge, naam (divine Name), devotion, Creator.
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine, as the sovereign Lord, consistently manifests devotees in every age and unfailingly safeguards their honor and dignity. This declaration affirms God's eternal commitment to protecting those who dedicate themselves to the Divine, ensuring their respect and standing are always upheld. It describes a continuous, unwavering divine action of creation and preservation.

Themes: Divine protection, devotees, honor, eternal commitment, divine sovereignty
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
The supplicant pleads with the Divine Master not to judge their past actions or karma, but instead to uphold the honor of the Divine's own servant. This is a plea for grace and mercy, asking the Divine to overlook human failings and extend protection and dignity based on the Divine's inherent nature of compassion, rather than on human merit. The speaker seeks divine intervention to preserve their spiritual standing.

Themes: divine grace, mercy, karma, surrender, divine protection, spiritual dignity, supplication
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
This line declares that the Divine Master accepts the plea of anyone who consistently begs for naam (the divine Name). It asserts that persistent, humble prayer for spiritual connection will always be granted, affirming the accessibility and responsiveness of the Divine to sincere devotion. The Master readily fulfills the desire for remembrance.

Themes: naam, prayer, divine grace, acceptance, devotion, spiritual seeking
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
This is a plea for the divine gift of naam (the divine Name), which brings contentment and satisfies the mind's insatiable hunger for worldly things. The speaker asks for spiritual fulfillment, seeking to quell the endless desires and cravings that plague the mind by receiving the divine essence.

Themes: naam, contentment, spiritual hunger, divine grace, mental peace
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
A supplicant begs for the divine Name (naam), repeatedly pleading for this spiritual sustenance. The act of begging itself is a form of devotion, expressing complete dependence on the Divine for all blessings and comfort. This repeated plea highlights the deep yearning for spiritual connection and the recognition that all true happiness comes from the Divine.

Themes: Supplication, naam, devotion, spiritual yearning, divine blessings
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
This is an entreaty to the Divine, Gopal Gobinde (Sustainer of the Earth, Cherisher of the Universe), for grace and mercy. The speaker implores the Divine to enable them to engage in simran (loving remembrance) of the naam (the divine Name), recognizing that this spiritual practice is a gift bestowed by divine will. It expresses a deep yearning for spiritual connection and acknowledges dependence on divine benevolence for its attainment.

Themes: Divine grace, simran, naam, spiritual yearning, dependence on God, Gopal Gobinde
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
This is a plea from a spiritual beggar to the Beloved Divine, asking for the gift of the divine Word, the Naam. The speaker, identifying as a humble seeker, implores the Lord to bestow this spiritual alms, expressing a deep yearning for divine grace and the sacred utterance.

Themes: begging, divine grace, Naam, spiritual seeking, surrender
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
This is a humble plea from a spiritual beggar, imploring the Divine for the gift of grace and mercy. The speaker, acknowledging their utter dependence, seeks divine benevolence, asking for the spiritual alms that only the Lord can bestow. It is an act of complete surrender, requesting the Lord's compassionate giving.

Themes: supplication, divine grace, spiritual begging, surrender, mercy
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
The mind and body flourish and become spiritually vibrant for anyone who receives even a single drop of the naam (the divine Name), which is like life-giving water. This describes the transformative spiritual renewal that results from even a small experience of the Divine.

Themes: naam, spiritual renewal, mind-body transformation, divine grace
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
The individual who partakes of the divine essence, the naam ras (the nectar of the divine Name), remains perpetually immersed in its vibrant hue. This spiritual absorption leads to an enduring state of being imbued with the divine, a continuous saturation in the love and presence of the Almighty. The act of drinking this spiritual elixir signifies a deep, transformative connection with the divine.

Themes: Naam ras, divine immersion, spiritual absorption, enduring connection, divine love.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
This passage instructs the seeker to continually sing the praises of the Divine, for kirtan (devotional singing) is the ambrosial essence that grants spiritual life. Engaging in this practice day and night leads to an unceasing inner resonance of spiritual bliss, a constant symphony of divine joy within the soul.

Themes: Kirtan, divine praise, spiritual life, inner joy, continuous remembrance.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
This is an instruction to one's own tongue, urging it to drink the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name), which bestows spiritual life. It is a call to engage in the loving remembrance of the Divine, finding sustenance and vitality in the recitation of God's Name. The tongue is implored to partake in this life-giving essence, transforming its function into a spiritual practice.

Themes: naam simran, spiritual sustenance, divine nectar, self-instruction, devotion
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
The devotee of God is completely absorbed and intoxicated by the divine essence, the naam rasayan (the elixir of the divine Name). This spiritual intoxication brings profound joy and a deep, abiding connection to the divine, filling the servant with the Lord's sublime presence. The mind is fully immersed in the divine Name, finding ultimate fulfillment and bliss.

Themes: Divine intoxication, naam simran, spiritual absorption, devotee's state, divine essence.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
This declares that spiritual nectar, the life-giving essence of the divine Name (naam), is imbibed through the Guru's wisdom, the Guru's Shabad. The speaker expresses profound devotion and surrender, sacrificing themselves to the divine Name, acknowledging it as the source of spiritual sustenance and ultimate refuge.

Themes: naam, Guru's Shabad, spiritual nectar, devotion, surrender, sacrifice
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
This line expresses a profound yearning for the divine Name (naam), describing it as an ambrosial essence, the most sublime and life-giving spiritual nectar. It poses a direct question, seeking instruction on the method or path to attain and experience this ultimate spiritual taste. The speaker is actively seeking the means to partake in this divine essence, emphasizing its supreme value and the desire to merge with it.

Themes: Naam, spiritual yearning, divine essence, attainment, spiritual nectar, seeking guidance.
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
This instruction to the soul, personified as a female friend, urges it to abandon the insipid and corrupting pursuits of worldly pleasures, which are likened to tasteless water. Instead, it should drink the naam (the divine Name), described as the supremely flavorful and life-giving nectar, emphasizing the spiritual nourishment and profound satisfaction found in divine remembrance over fleeting material gratifications.

Themes: naam, spiritual nourishment, renunciation, worldly pleasures, divine remembrance
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
This declares that the agony of separation from the Divine, a spiritual yearning likened to a venomous snake, takes root in the mind, rendering all worldly remedies and incantations utterly ineffective. It asserts that once this profound longing for the Divine is established, no external mantra or ritual can alleviate its intensity or provide solace. The pain of spiritual longing is a unique affliction that transcends conventional solutions.

Themes: spiritual yearning, divine separation, ineffectiveness of rituals, mind's suffering, longing for God
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
The speaker declares to their mother that life without the divine Name (naam) is unbearable, expressing an intense longing for spiritual connection. The soul is distressed and restless without the remembrance of the Divine, emphasizing a profound dependence on the Supreme Soul for true existence and inner peace.

Themes: longing for the divine, spiritual dependence, naam simran, inner peace, soul's distress
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
The speaker's mind is filled with an intense longing, a deep love and affection, for the Divine, expressing a profound spiritual yearning to unite with the Beloved. This passionate desire to meet God has taken root within their consciousness, becoming the central focus of their inner life.

Themes: spiritual yearning, divine love, longing for union, mind's devotion
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
This declares the soul's intense longing for a vision of the Divine, expressing a profound spiritual thirst. It likens the mind's fervent desire for God's presence to the desperate need of a parched person for water, emphasizing an essential, life-sustaining yearning for the Divine darshan (blessed vision). The soul is consumed by this spiritual hunger, seeking the Lord above all else.

Themes: Spiritual longing, divine vision, essential need, spiritual thirst, yearning for God.
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
The soul, feeling utterly alone and abandoned in the world, cries out in distress, acknowledging that only the Beloved Divine cares for its plight and offers true solace. It expresses a profound sense of isolation and a desperate yearning for the Divine's compassionate attention, recognising the futility of seeking help elsewhere.

Themes: divine compassion, spiritual loneliness, yearning for God, refuge in the Divine
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
The mind of the fortunate devotee is filled with dispassion towards worldly attachments, and an intense longing for the blessed vision (darshan) of the Divine. This spiritual yearning arises from a deep love for the Divine, prompting the soul to seek direct experience of the Beloved.

Themes: spiritual yearning, divine love, detachment, darshan, blessed vision
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
This is an impassioned plea from the soul, the bride, to the Divine Husband, asking Him to return to the heart's home after a long separation. The soul yearns for reunion with the Divine, specifically requesting this union be facilitated through the Guru's Shabad (the divine Word), which is the means of spiritual connection and merging with the Lord.

Themes: Divine union, separation from God, Guru's Shabad, spiritual longing, heart as home.
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The soul-bride acknowledges that her separation from the divine Husband, the bestower of all comforts, is not His fault but entirely due to her own misdeeds and spiritual failings. She takes full responsibility for her estrangement, recognizing her unworthiness and the purity of the divine source of peace.

Themes: divine grace, personal responsibility, separation from the divine, spiritual failings, self-blame
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
The seeker implores the Guru, the divine teacher, to enter the sanctuary of their heart, longing to hear the praises of the Divine. This is a fervent plea for spiritual guidance and the transformative power of sacred sound, seeking to fill the inner self with the glory of the Divine. The soul yearns for the Guru's presence to awaken divine remembrance.

Themes: Guru's presence, divine praise, spiritual yearning, inner sanctuary, transformative listening
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
This is an intimate, yearning plea from the devotee's soul, inviting the Beloved Lord, the cherished Ram, to reside within their heart. It expresses a deep longing for the divine presence to dwell internally, seeking an indwelling of the divine within the devotee's very being. The soul implores the beloved to come and make their heart a home, signifying a profound desire for spiritual union and constant communion.

Themes: Divine indwelling, spiritual longing, intimate prayer, divine presence, heart as dwelling.
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
This is a plea from the soul-bride to the Divine Husband, asking for His mercy and presence within the heart. It expresses a deep longing for spiritual union, imploring the Beloved to return and reside within the inner sanctuary of the self, signifying a desire for constant awareness of the Divine.

Themes: Divine mercy, spiritual union, inner dwelling, longing for God, soul-bride.
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
The soul-bride implores the captivating Divine, Mohan, to manifest within the sanctuary of her heart, pleading for the indwelling presence of the Beloved. This is an earnest supplication for spiritual union, a fervent prayer for the Divine to reside within one's inner being, transforming the self into a sacred abode.

Themes: Divine presence, spiritual union, inner sanctuary, supplication, Mohan (captivating Divine).
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The divine Beloved has manifested within the seeker's heart, transforming it into a sacred home. This declaration expresses the profound joy and spiritual fulfillment experienced when the Divine, perceived as a cherished friend, arrives and takes residence within one's inner being, signifying a state of union and intimate connection.

Themes: Divine presence, inner experience, spiritual union, heart as home
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
This scripture uses the metaphor of a flowering plant to illustrate the progression of spiritual practice and its rewards. Early devotion, like a flower, is beautiful but not yet complete. The true fruit of spiritual effort, the ultimate spiritual realization and connection with the Divine, comes from sustained practice, particularly in the ambrosial hours of dawn (Amrit Vela). It instructs that consistent spiritual effort yields profound spiritual fulfillment.

Themes: spiritual practice, devotion, spiritual reward, Amrit Vela, metaphor
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
This is an admonition to the self, urging an awakening from the slumber of maya (worldly attachment) and a call to engage in simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine. It questions the futility of wasting life in spiritual heedlessness and implores one to rise and meditate on the Lord, rather than remaining lost in the illusion of worldly desires.

Themes: Admonition to self, awakening, simran, maya, futility of worldly attachment
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
This is an instruction to begin each day by remembering the divine Name (naam) and meditating on the Guru's feet, which represents reverent contemplation of the Guru's wisdom and guidance. It emphasizes the spiritual discipline of rising early to connect with the Divine and honor the Guru's role in leading one to naam. This practice is presented as foundational for spiritual growth and maintaining humility.

Themes: naam simran, Guru's wisdom, daily discipline, spiritual practice, humility, divine connection
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
This is an instruction to rise before dawn and engage in simran (loving remembrance) of naam (the divine Name), urging continuous, unbroken devotion throughout both day and night. It emphasizes the practice of early morning meditation as a foundational discipline for constant spiritual remembrance, making the remembrance of the Divine the central purpose of one's entire existence.

Themes: naam simran, early morning devotion, continuous remembrance, spiritual discipline, divine worship
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
The soul, like a rainbird, cries out to the Divine during the ambrosial hours of early morning, and this heartfelt plea is heard and acknowledged in the Divine Court. This expresses the efficacy of sincere prayer and the accessibility of the Divine through devotion, particularly during the sacred time of dawn. The Divine listens to and accepts the supplications of the devoted.

Themes: prayer, divine grace, ambrosial hours, devotion, divine court
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Chanting the praises of the Divine cools the heart and brings peace to the mind, creating a state of inner tranquility and contentment. This spiritual practice of singing the Lord's glories soothes the soul and establishes a profound sense of well-being, leading to a serene and joyful existence.

Themes: Divine praise, inner peace, spiritual tranquility, contentment, devotional singing
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing the praises of the Divine (kirtan) is the true yoga, uniting the soul with the Divine and bringing both worldly contentment and spiritual detachment. This practice fulfills the purpose of human life, achieving union with the Divine through devotional song.

Themes: kirtan, yoga, divine union, spiritual practice, praise
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
This is a personal declaration of constant devotion, expressing the speaker's continuous engagement in naam simran (loving remembrance of the divine Name) and kirtan (singing praises of the Divine). The speaker commits to ceaselessly chanting and glorifying the divine Name, making it a perpetual practice of spiritual remembrance and adoration.

Themes: naam simran, kirtan, constant devotion, spiritual practice, divine praise
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
This instruction encourages the seeker to rise early and join the sangat (company of the devout) to continually sing the praises of the Divine. It describes the sweet, unstruck sound of the Shabad (Divine Word) as a constant melody, urging its regular, harmonious recitation as a spiritual practice. The line emphasizes consistent devotional effort within the community.

Themes: Divine praise, daily practice, unstruck sound, sangat, spiritual discipline.
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
This is an instruction to the devout to continually sing the praises of the Master of the Universe, to always recount the virtues of the Lord of the World. It is an exhortation to remember and glorify the Divine, urging constant recitation of God's excellences.

Themes: praising the Divine, constant remembrance, spiritual instruction, glorifying God
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
Sing the praises of the Creator with a mind free from worldly desires, for through this devotional singing, even a moment of naam simran (loving remembrance of the divine Name) brings liberation from vices and worldly attachments. This instruction encourages continuous remembrance of the Divine as the path to spiritual freedom and release from maya (worldly illusion).

Themes: Naam simran, liberation, devotion, freedom from desire, divine praise.
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The mind finds everything You do to be sweet and good, accepting all divine actions as inherently beneficial and just. This is a declaration of complete surrender to the divine will, expressing a state of profound contentment and trust in the divine plan, where no complaint or grievance is ever raised against the divine.

Themes: divine will, surrender, contentment, trust, acceptance, no complaints
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
The actions of the Divine Friend are perceived as sources of comfort and well-being, bringing peace and contentment to the observer. The speaker finds joy and solace in the divine will, experiencing every deed of the Beloved as a blessing that brings profound happiness. This expresses a state of complete acceptance and trust in the divine plan.

Themes: Divine will, spiritual comfort, acceptance, trust in God, inner peace
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Embracing the divine will of God brings complete peace, joy, and all spiritual pleasures. Accepting the Lord's command as sweet and beneficial leads to a state of perfect happiness and auspiciousness, transforming one's experience of life into continuous bliss.

Themes: Divine will, acceptance, peace, joy, spiritual pleasure, auspiciousness.
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The divine Creator possesses the absolute power to create and destroy all things in an instant, holding all decisions and outcomes within the divine will. This asserts the omnipotence and ultimate control of the divine over all existence, emphasising that all power resides solely with the Creator.

Themes: Divine omnipotence, divine will, creation and destruction, ultimate control.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
This instruction urges the mind to constantly remember and meditate upon naam (the divine Name), assuring that all endeavors will be successfully completed. It declares that focusing on the Divine presence ensures the resolution and fulfillment of all tasks and purposes in life. The practice of simran (loving remembrance) is presented as the ultimate means to achieve success and completion in all undertakings.

Themes: naam simran, divine remembrance, success, fulfillment, spiritual practice
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
This instruction to one's own mind promises that all endeavors will be brought to fruition and successfully completed if one continually sings the praises of the Divine. Reciting the virtues of the Lord ensures that all tasks reach their intended conclusion, yielding positive results and fulfilling one's purpose.

Themes: Divine praise, successful completion, spiritual practice, mind's instruction, divine virtues.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
This instruction to the mind declares that meditating on naam (the divine Name) is the sole purpose of human life, ensuring all endeavors are fulfilled and life's ultimate objective is achieved. It asserts that through devotion to the divine Name, every task finds its proper resolution and success.

Themes: naam simran, purpose of life, spiritual success, divine grace
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
This declares that all of one's tasks and objectives are perfectly accomplished when the Divine Will is aligned with one's efforts, asserting that divine pleasure ensures the successful resolution of all undertakings. It expresses a profound trust in the benevolent power of the Divine, affirming that when God is pleased, every aspect of life falls into perfect order.

Themes: Divine Will, successful completion, divine pleasure, trust in God, alignment with the divine.
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
This declares the ultimate outcome of spiritual devotion: all aspirations are completely fulfilled, and the devotee is permanently freed from suffering. It describes a state of perfect contentment and liberation from all distress, achieved through divine grace and spiritual union.

Themes: spiritual fulfillment, liberation from suffering, divine grace, ultimate contentment
